god_relations.note: Boukman invokes the creator to command vengeance, guide rebel arms and aid liberation.
Later commemorative and ritual interpretations associate this war spirit with Boukman’s foundational ceremony.
Some modern commemorations honor Legba, although no early account places him in Boukman’s ceremony.

god_relations.myth: Makandal assumes Ayizan’s herbal and initiatory authority
god_relations.note: Depestre poetically overlays Makandal with Ayizan’s authority over initiation and medicinal herbs.

god_relations.myth: Mandate to destroy whites and return Blacks to Africa
god_relations.note: Later legend claims Petro spirits mandated Makandal’s anticolonial mission.

Agaté.myth: Makandal mentors Agaté as an Assassin
Agaté.note: Agaté remembers Makandal as his Assassin mentor.

Damballah.note: Recent variants claim Damballah possessed an attendee, without support from the principal early narratives.

Dominique.note: Augustin invents Dominique as Makandal and Wamba’s son.

Satan/the Devil.note: Evangelical teaching claims Boukman exchanged service to Satan for Haiti’s freedom.

Ti Noël.myth: Makandal instructs Ti Noël before his execution
Ti Noël.note: Makandal instructs and inspires Ti Noël, who witnesses his career and execution.

Wamba.note: Augustin invents Wamba as Makandal’s wife.

Èzili Dantò.note: Later tradition links her possession of Cécile Fatiman and receipt of the pig sacrifice to Boukman’s ceremony.

Èzili Je Wouj.note: Some Haitian religious accounts substitute this fiery Èzili form as the priestess’s possessing spirit.

“The god of the whites”.note: Boukman denounces this god as commanding crime and thirsting for enslaved people’s tears.
